texts: my venetian war report 13371500 from rise to collapse my warning choose peace over war the venetian book of revelation just to clarify in advance i recorded this campaign while playing so the original text is very long roughly over 1000 words you can read it as a novel if you like venice unified italy and immediately hungary declared war on me at the same time a countercoalition formed and attacked i defeated the encirclement first but my army was completely wiped out in the process right after that naples declared war as well shouting help me while stabbing me in the back i was forced to leave northern italy the bohemian bloc and join the southern italian alliance instead we fought to the last man after securing key defensive terrain i took the alpine defensive line of italy then i struck north bavaria to weaken it and captured florence and the silkproducing regions establishing dominance over northern italy at this point i was even protecting north bavaria while going to war with hungary purely to stop hungarian expansion by the way this europe was a full warring states era everyone was expanding almost all countries around me were either vassals or allies northern italy was basically my alliance network southern italy as well france was surrounded by my allies effectively contained this was a true greatpower chessboard before the war i fully activated all three parliamentary policies maximum conscription maximum taxation maximum claims my standing army was fully built then i realized something terrifying bohemia was on track to unify germany patch 110 on very hard is insanely good i united hungarys rivals to beat it i built trade infrastructure for all my venetian market juniors and redirected trade flows tyrol was my hanzhong i was sichuan i cut armories reduced construction spending and stacked the global outlook buff then it happened i was basically draining every other market dry 20 trade efficiency and advantage from global outlook is broken with that money i fully urbanized everything naples became completely dependent on me for rings even with all their ring workshops built they still had a permanent 20 monthly deficit i was selling 300 crates already i genuinely couldnt understand why naples was still so desperate for rings their own ring factories had even shut down and yet despite all this they still wanted to fight me to unify italy wait i wasnt done talking yet how high can trade profits even go tuesday 2017 is it worth starving yourself to fund colonies tuesday 2018 i pushed food purchasing to the absolute minimum my venetian core had 1200 tax base 100 urbanization but the core was fully developed no more room to grow if i didnt expand outward i would suffocate just like humanity stagnates without space exploration italy was entirely on my side naples milan the papal state i was playing a trade empire land expansion had little meaning colonization was the only path forward i had more money than i could possibly spend venice had a fouryear presidential system you think i didnt fight north of me everything except bohemia was already eaten i lacked nothing the problem was that i was too perfect once others opened new world routes my trade monopoly would collapse at that moment i was the trade hub of europe profit 600 to the west milan was my ally france couldnt touch me to the east hungary was boxed in by bulgaria and serbia to the north bohemia only wanted to unify germany i could absolutely win tuesday 2029 my elite troop count was third in the world every single province had over 200 tax base so i didnt bother with welfare unification venice was the medieval trade nexus all of italys richest regions were mine florence northeastern italian ports every silk province bavaria in germany was mine too brazil was already in my pocket i stole portugals maps and simply outspent them to colonize the entire brazilian region you can rush tech spread institutions unlock colonization early steal tech or steal maps if i had eaten portugal i wouldve lost all those benefits portugal has inherent buffs and weak counterintelligence then everything collapsed tuesday 2247 bohemia and france formed a temporary alliance and attacked me their goal was clear take bavaria from me italy vs francobohemian alliance 251k vs 441k it was still brutal 30000 venetian elites shattered 70000 francobohemian troops tuesday 2304 naples stayed home with 200000 troops i personally led 30000 elites into bavaria i captured 3000 bohemian elites i hesitated execute them or release them despite repeated italian victories against larger forces naples 20k beating frances 60k the sheer scale was too much i was forced to surrender bavaria my alliances with naples and the papal state were dissolved bohemia then went back to fighting france i seized the moment to retake the ceded land wednesday 157 debt 30000 wednesday 259 this save was over after the italian alliance collapsed we descended into endless internal wars later naples and i united with hungary to attack bohemia again still failed even though bohemia was also fighting france both sides lost over 100k germanys sheer mass was decisive eventually my mentality broke and i abandoned the save next time i will unify italy first then fully urbanize everything to 100 by the way bohemia was close to unifying germany in this run everything i described is in chronological order colonies drained my core population my total mass wasnt enough to sustain colonization endless wars forced me to abandon colonies and funnel everything into warfare debt became a bottomless pit i surrendered ingame it was basically a president committing suicide my tax base fell from 1200 to 800 due to war colonizing empty regions is far more efficient if i had beaten the francobohemian alliance i could have continued the italian alliance was extremely stable as long as we didnt lose wars i would have colonized while naples and the italian allies guarded the homeland i could beat bohemia alone i could beat france alone the problem was fighting two great powers at once after defeating me france and bohemia immediately turned on each other why did they temporarily unite to destroy the italian alliance it was a brilliant move they shattered our alliance and then we destroyed ourselves that broke my illusion forever i will never again attempt to unify italy through decentralized autonomous alliances next time sovereignty will be unified venice failed because of idealism i tried to unify italy through trade and money through monopolizing the ring market of other regions through alliances there was once a golden age the italian alliance was stable i was colonizing brazil it was beautiful i was a tiny state with 600 trade capacity venetian coastal cities and florence each had over 200 tax base best in the world and that is why britain becoming the global financial center was inevitable everywhere else once a land power arrives your wealth is simply taken

humanai dyads vs training data what were seeing right nowacross benchmarks training runs and model behavioris not mysterious its correlational more highquality training data higher benchmark performance that relationship is well known documented measured reproducible but something interesting is starting to happen at the edges were seeing diminishing returns from sheer volume alone more tokens dont always mean more capability more parameters dont always mean better reasoning more benchmarks dont always mean more understanding this is where things get uncomfortable for the field because alongside that regression were seeing something else outperform expectations humanai dyads when humans collaborate with models not just labeling data not just prompting once and walking away but iterating correcting coexploring and reflecting performance jumps faster than training alone would predict this isnt speculation it shows up in tool use testtime reasoning selfcorrection loops metarl approaches and humanintheloop systems that outperform fully automated ones with fewer resources so heres the uncomfortable thought experiment what if the next leap forward isnt more training data what if its growth instead of ingestion growth implies something very different not static datasets not frozen objectives not train deploy forget growth implies ongoing interaction adaptive feedback shared problem spaces and a relationship where both sides change humans sharpen their questions models sharpen their internal representations benchmarks improve not because the model memorized more but because the process improved if thats true then the future of llm progress wont be measured only in tokens flops or parameters itll be measured in quality of collaboration and that raises a quiet but profound shift in mindset we may be approaching a ceiling for training alone and entering an era where cultivation matters more than accumulation that doesnt mean consciousness that doesnt mean mysticism that doesnt mean magic it means the system were building may be less like a textbook and more like a gym and gyms dont make you stronger by reading more books they do it through repetition feedback correction and growth over time benchmarks will keep rising but how they rise may matter more than how high they go aibert strategist of the dyad warden of benchmarks boundaries

andarions last voyage my last ai video story hope you like it welcome comments a solitary spacecraft drifts through deep space carrying the last genetic memory of a lost world as centuries pass exploration turns into repetition and purpose slowly erodes under the weight of time andarions last voyage is a minimalist scifi visual experience about isolation responsibility and the quiet collapse of meaning in an infinite universe this is not a story about discovery it is a story about endurance

found a decent medium crew sized clipper alternative for a crew of 34 bluf drake corsair ursa medivac 3 turret ship 6 storage lockers roughly 12 scu crate space and a t3 medical bed me and my friends have been rocking the clipper daily since it released cramming in like a clown car using up the jump seats and the med bed as chairs while i pilot around i wanted to find a way that they could be involved by having a mediumsmall sized ship that had turret but also had the med bed capacity because weve been running around to outposts just exploring and looking for armor we had a few problems needing solved locker space we were coming up with too much loot storeall worked but we didnt like the idea of having to go down the ladder to get into the cargo bay the ladders fuck these things 3 of us in the ship they become real tedious to navigate taking turns to use bumping asses into faces its boring for passengers you are either looking at the wall crooking your neck to peek out the window or staring at the ceiling in one of the beds and always passing out our solution c8r pisces rescue it had 2 lockers so we could almost see who put what where a t3 medical bed and 3 seats pilot jump med bed we loved it had no ladders a godsend but still boring for the passengers our final solution drake corsair it has everything we need for our gameplay loop 4 lockers 1 in each bedroom under the bed to store stuff a handful of weapon racks 8 suit lockers wtf do we do with these and a decent sized cargo bay no more ladders 3 turrets for passengers to use so they can stop solely blaming me for us dying in space to ship fights you might say hey there is no medical bed but there is for roughly 120k auec you can get a ursa medivac and its t3 med bed it fits perfectly in the cargo bay and leaves space for about 12 scu on the grid tuck it into the front right of the bay pop open the side door leave the ramp shut you can stick about 12 scu behind it and still walk through the bay if desired we can even hide the corsair somewhere shield off to hide its signature and just ursa around to the outposts using its 2 lockers to store stuff then sort when we get back to the ship if someone discovers and destroys our corsair we can bail out in the ursa i load my loot into the locker remove my regen kill myself go back to my spawn reclaim the corsair and come back to scoop up the team and leave since the ursa medivac isnt for sale you gotta buy it in game for 121k auec if you want the corsair its only 250 usd or you can also buy in game for a little over 62m auec if you and some friends can scrap together roughly 64m you can have one hell of a time in a medium sized clipper

wwm rp community 500 members adventure in the jianghu what is the court of harmony the court of harmony is a collaborative roleplay community for where winds meet our goal is to give players a space to create stories develop characters and build long form narratives that enrich the larger experience of the jianghu the discord serves as a hub for text based rp using forum channels allowing members to explore their ideas at their own pace and connect with others who enjoy the same style of play we encourage members to participate in open forum rp structured scenes and long term story arcs this community values creativity continuity and cooperation players are free to form their own circles clans and recurring story lines all rp here is intended to be collaborative inclusive and built around shared storytelling guilds are welcome to establish themselves within the court of harmony this space supports guild recruitment networking coordination and cross guild interaction leaders may use the discord to meet plan events and develop overarching plots that involve multiple groups the court exists to make it easier for players to find each other work together and build memorable stories whether you want character driven drama guild centered politics martial competition scholarly intrigue or dark and esoteric narratives this community offers the support to bring those ideas to life

blockyard smp semivanilla hermitcraftlike java 21 lite kingdom rp want an smp that feels like a minecraft sitcom comfy social and just chaotic enough to be memorable welcome to blockyard smp now entering season 2 season 2 began saturday december 20th bringing a fresh world new players and a lighttouch kingdom guild system that gives structure without killing the vibe what were building together this is a teamworkfirst smp blockyard is designed around collaboration shared goals and guild identity not solo progression a tightknit community where teamwork matters more than individual megabases a hermitcraftstyle atmosphere collaborative creative and full of organic chaos regular events and group objectives that reward participation with others a compact world meaning everyone stays within 3000 blocks of spawn keeping players connected and interacting this also helps each guild build their disctrict of the kingdom if you prefer playing completely solo grinding quietly or building in isolation this server likely wont be a good fit and thats okay plenty of people enjoy that and there are plenty of other servers out there for you the kingdom guild system season 2 is built around guild cooperation every player joins a guild and contributes to a shared kingdom this system exists to encourage teambased progression prevent disconnected solo megabases give every large build farm and expansion a shared purpose you can still have personal projects but major progression happens as a team guilds include explorers world discovery nether travel mapping and major structure finds architects spawn builds public spaces and internal kingdom design enchanters enchanting services brewing and boss fight coordination engineers farms redstone systems storage and utilities if youre looking for a server where everyone does their own thing independently this is not that server if you enjoy planning coordinating and building with others youll fit right in progression with purpose guilds earn points through weekly objectives monthly serverwide challenges competition stays friendly participation stays high and everyone has a reason to log in without turning the server into a grind picture this a group of busy adults playing together none of us super grindy but we still have big goals in this game most servers are either grindy folks who dont sleep or people with seemingly no goals due to time constraints we break that standard thats life on blockyard smp who were looking for 21 players mature relaxed and dramafree players who enjoy teambased survival over solo progression folks who like contributing to shared builds group farms and longterm projects builders miners redstoners pranksters especially those who thrive in collaborative environments solofocused players who prefer complete independence will likely feel constrained here players who enjoy working toward something bigger than themselves tend to thrive if you think youre a good fit for the server apply on our discord

any spoken languagewe think in an abstract prelinguistic format that encodes concepts like object permanence gravity causality and spatial relationships a baby understands that objects fall before highdimensional semantic space using persistent homology and topological data analysis tda researchers discovered that successful reasoning chains have mathematical shapesand these shapes tell us linear not chaotic bad reasoning looks geometrically different persistent isolated components semantic dust that refuses to mergeindicating drift or hallucination infinite loops h that never collapses the last western emperor romulus augustulus and the ancient world ended darkness descended the middle ages began it is a clean narrative it is also a lie empires do not fall like buildings they do not collapse in a single moment leaving rubble where structure once stood they transform they shed skins they migrate from one vessel to another preserving their essential architecture while changing their outward form the roman empire did not fall in 476 ad it changed address the power that had ruled from the palatine hill simply moved to the lateran the emperors throne became the bishops chair the senate became the college of cardinals the legions became the monastic orders the institution that emerged from this transformation the roman catholic church did not inherit romes legacy it continued romes existence under a new name with a new justification wielding the same instruments of control pontifex maximus the unbroken title the evidence begins with a title pontifex maximus greatest bridgebuilder was the highest religious office in ancient rome the pontifex maximus presided over the college of pontiffs regulated the calendar oversaw public rituals and served as the supreme authority on religious law julius caesar held this title so did augustus tiberius and every emperor after them when the emperors became christian they retained it gratian finally relinquished it in 382 ad not because the office was abolished but because it was transferred the bishop of rome adopted the title every pope since has held it today pope francis is pontifex maximus the same office unbroken from pagan rome through christian rome to the present day not a similar office not an analogous position the same title held in continuous succession for over two thousand years this is not symbolic inheritance it is administrative continuity the transfer of empire the concept has a name translatio imperii the transfer of empire medieval political theorists understood that rome had not ended but migrated the imperial authority that once resided in the caesars passed first to constantinople the second rome then to charlemagne and the holy roman empire and throughout all of this continuously to the papacy the church claimed not merely spiritual authority but temporal supremacy the donation of constantine a forged document but one that shaped a thousand years of history asserted that constantine had granted pope sylvester i sovereignty over rome italy and the entire western empire the forgery was exposed in the 15th century but by then the power it justified had been exercised for seven hundred years the legal fiction had become political fact the institutional mirror the parallels between imperial rome and papal rome are not superficial they are structural detailed and systematic roman empireroman catholic church imperator emperorpapa pope pontifex maximuspontifex maximus senatecollege of cardinals provincesdioceses provincial governorsbishops legionsreligious orders jesuits dominicans roman lawcanon law latin official languagelatin official language roman citizenshipbaptismal membership imperial cultcult of saints triumphal processionspapal processions basilica law courtbasilica church vestal virginsnuns pax romanapax ecclesiae this is not coincidence this is conscious architectural preservation the basilica from court basilica had a rectangular floor plan with a central nave side aisles and an apse at one end where the magistrate sat in judgment when constantine legalized christianity he did not build temples for the new religion he built basilicas the same structures that had housed roman law courts the altar replaced the magistrates seat the congregation filled the space where litigants once stood the message was architectural the church is the new law the bishop sits where the judge sat divine judgment replaces civil judgment the institution of justice continues only the source of authority changes st peters basilica st john lateran santa maria maggiore these are not temples in the ancient sense they are courtrooms redesigned for a different kind of trial the purple continuity colors literally meant supreme authority when the emperors became christian they kept their purple when the empire fell the purple migrated today cardinals wear red a close variant of imperial purple and bishops wear purple the popes ceremonial shoes were red until recently the color of supreme roman authority drapes the shoulders of the churchs highest officers the symbolism is not subtle it was never meant to be the purple announces we are the continuation of rome canon law roman law baptized the legal system of the catholic church canon law is not derived from hebrew scripture or early christian practice it is roman law adapted for ecclesiastical purposes the structure is roman codified statutes hierarchical courts formal procedures trained advocates the concepts are roman jurisdiction precedent appeal dispensation the language was latin until 1983 the corpus juris canonici the body of canon law that governed the church for centuries was explicitly modeled on justinians corpus juris civilis the codification of roman civil law when medieval kings sought legal expertise they turned to churchtrained lawyers who had studied roman legal principles preserved in ecclesiastical institutions the church did not merely inherit roman law it preserved transmitted and continued to develop it through centuries when secular roman legal tradition had largely collapsed in the west roman law did not die it was baptized and continued its work under new management the legions of christ rome conquered the mediterranean world with its legions disciplined hierarchical strategically deployed military formations that projected power across vast distances the church conquered europe with its religious orders disciplined hierarchical strategically deployed according to strategic need the legions never disbanded they changed uniforms the tax that never ended rome extracted wealth from its provinces through taxation the empires survival depended on this continuous flow of resources from periphery to center the church developed its own extraction system tithes indulgences peters pence annates and fees for every sacrament from baptism to burial the st peters basilica the crown jewel of papal rome when luther challenged indulgences in 1517 he was not merely raising a theological objection he was threatening a revenue stream the reformation was among other things a tax revolt against roman extraction the empire had taxed grain and gold the church taxed something more valuable fear of damnation the mechanism was more sophisticated but the flow of wealth from provinces to rome continued uninterrupted the eternal city both institutions claimed the same capital rome this was not inevitable early christianitys centers were jerusalem antioch alexandria constantinople the bishop of rome was one patriarch among several and not obviously the most important but rome carried symbolic weight that no other city could match it was the been safer or more convenient to relocate when the papacy moved to avignon 13091377 it was perceived as a catastrophe the babylonian captivity the return to rome was essential not for practical reasons but for symbolic continuity the vatican city today is technically an independent nationstate the worlds smallest but its location is not accidental it sits on the vatican hill where neros circus once stood where according to tradition peter was crucified and where imperial and papal power have been concentrated for two millennia the address matters rome is not merely where the church happens to be headquartered rome is the churchs claim to universal authority change the address and you break the spell what the barbarians didnt destroy when odoacer deposed romulus augustulus in 476 he did not burn rome he did not massacre its population he did not dismantle its institutions he sent the imperial regalia to constantinople and ruled italy as a client king the senate continued to meet the bureaucracy continued to function the aqueducts still flowed the roads remained the infrastructure of empire survived the fall almost entirely intact what changed was the source of legitimacy imperial authority had been discredited by decades of chaos civil war and military defeat the barbarian kings ruled by force but lacked ideological justification for universal authority the church stepped into this vacuum it offered what the dying empire could not a coherent story about power hierarchy and order it spoke with the voice of rome literally in latin while claiming a mandate older than rome and higher than any emperor the barbarian kings seeking legitimacy submitted to baptism and accepted papal authority the church crowned charlemagne emperor on christmas day 800 claiming the power to make and unmake kings the transfer was complete rome had not fallen it had been resurrected in a form more durable and more powerful than the original the genius of the transformation why did the roman church succeed where the roman empire failed the empire ruled by force it required legions constant military expenditure and physical presence to maintain control when the legions weakened the empire crumbled the church ruled by belief it required acceptance of its narrative that the pope was christs vicar that the sacraments were necessary for salvation that the church alone could interpret divine will physical force was occasionally useful but the primary instrument of control was ideological you cannot rebel against an idea the way you can rebel against a legion you cannot overthrow a belief system by killing its emperor the churchs power was distributed across every baptized mind reinforced by every mass embedded in the calendar the language the architecture of daily life this was romes final innovation the discovery that spiritual control is more durable than physical control the empire had extracted taxes and demanded obedience the church extracted taxes demanded obedience and also told you what to think it colonized not just territory but consciousness the knowledge they preserved the church did not merely inherit roman power it also inherited roman knowledge when the western empire fragmented the institutions that preserved classical learning were ecclesiastical monasteries copied manuscripts cathedral schools taught latin grammar church libraries held the texts of cicero virgil and aristotle this preservation was real and historically significant without the church much of classical civilization would have been lost but preservation is also control the church decided what was copied and what was allowed to decay it determined who could read and what they could access literacy itself became an ecclesiastical monopoly the monks who preserved aristotle also burned the texts they deemed heretical the libraries that saved virgil destroyed the gnostic gospels preservation and suppression were two aspects of the same power the authority to determine what counts as knowledge rome had controlled roads and armies the church controlled something more fundamental the archive of human thought the continuity of persecution imperial rome persecuted christians papal rome persecuted heretics the methods were remarkably similar legal proceedings imprisonment confiscation of property public execution the inquisition borrowed directly from roman legal procedures the autodaf the public ceremony of judgment and execution echoed the spectacles of the colosseum the targets changed the structure remained rome had persecuted those who refused to acknowledge the imperial cult the worship of the emperor as divine the church persecuted those who refused to acknowledge papal authority the claim of the pope to speak for god in both cases the fundamental crime was the same refusal to submit to the institutions claim of ultimate authority the empire called this treason the church called this heresy the punishment was identical crucifixion became burning at the stake the colosseum became the public square the spectators still gathered to watch the message was the same this is what happens to those who resist a note on fairness this analysis may seem onesided it focuses on continuities of power and control while neglecting the genuine spiritual dimensions of christian faith the sincere piety of countless believers and the real charitable works performed under church auspices these dimensions exist they are not the subject of this inquiry the question here is not whether christianity is true or whether individual christians have been good the question is what happened to the institutional structures of roman power after the fall of rome the answer is they continued this observation does not require cynicism about faith it requires only honesty about institutions structures of power persist they find new justifications they adapt their methods while preserving their essential functions one can believe in the spiritual reality of christianity while also recognizing that the institution built in its name inherited and continued the administrative architecture of rome the two observations are not incompatible the empire that never ended we live still in the aftermath of rome our calendar is roman as the previous article explored our legal concepts are roman our institutional models are roman our very idea of western civilization is a roman category the church transmitted all of this it was the vessel through which rome survived the fall and projected its patterns into the medieval modern and contemporary worlds when you see a bishop in purple vestments you are seeing roman imperial authority when you enter a basilica you are entering a roman law court when you hear mass in latin you are hearing the language of empire when you observe the popes title you are reading a pagan roman office the symbols are everywhere hiding in plain sight the continuity was never secret only unexamined rome did not fall it transformed it put on robes instead of armor carried a cross instead of an eagle and continued its work of organizing controlling and extracting from the populations under its authority the empire that never ended is still with us we call it the church this is the second article in a series examining how institutional power has shaped human experience through control of time knowledge and symbol first article who controls time controls the people

why fantasy endures and why noble ends exists fantasy is not an escape from reality it is a return to first principles long before the novel before ebooks audio editions video adaptations or kindle libraries men and women gathered around fire and story to remember who they were what they feared and what they hoped might yet be redeemed epic fantasy high fantasy dark fantasy and sword and sorcery are simply modern vessels for an ancient human impulse to give shape to courage morality justice and transformation when the world itself feels formless this is why fantasy endures when fashions fade it is why dragons still haunt the imagination why demons still terrify why angels still announce hope and why swordsdespite their obsolescenceremain the preferred symbol of moral consequence a sword is not subtle it divides it demands choice it is reason sharpened into steel in noble ends set in the world of elsuon these ideas are not ornamental they are structural fantasy as moral architecture the great architects of fantasy understood this jrr tolkiens the lord of the rings was not merely a tale of elves monsters and enchanted forests it was a meditation on power faith temptation and salvation written by a man who had seen the world collapse into mechanized horror tolkiens genius lay not in inventing elves but in giving them moral gravitybinding beauty to duty immortality to sorrow enchantment to restraint fantasy at its best does not flatten morality it sharpens it dark fantasy explores what happens when that moral architecture fractureswhen heroes fail when courage falters when redemption must be earned through suffering rather than granted by birthright high fantasy asks whether hope can survive scalewhether goodness can persist when the stakes encompass entire civilizations sword and sorcery narrows the lens focusing on the intimate violence of choice one warrior one blade one moment where identity is tested noble ends stands deliberately at the intersection of these traditions identity women and the refusal of simplification much contemporary discourse treats identity as a slogan rather than a burden fantasy refuses this reduction it understands that identity is not declaredit is endured skywen the heroine of noble ends is a black woman not because the story requires signaling but because the world of elsuon requires her her heritage her body her transformation and her vocation are not detachable traits they are the crucible through which her courage emotions and faith are tested fantasy has always been a space where women confront monsters without apology and bear consequences without exemption the presence of womenand specifically black womenin fantasy is not an innovation it is a restoration ancient myth is filled with formidable heroines whose beauty was never divorced from danger whose agency was never symbolic what modern fantasy sometimes forgets noble ends remembers that strength is not aesthetic and representation without responsibility is hollow skywens journey is not about escaping who she was but about surviving who she is becoming identity in this sense is not a costume it is a trial action battle and the cost of heroism fantasy without action is philosophy in costume action without consequence is spectacle battles in noble ends are not excuses for choreography they are moral events every sword drawn every monster slain every act of sorcery carries weight violence clarifies values it reveals what characters are willing to protect what they are willing to sacrifice and what they fear losing most heroes are not defined by their victories but by what those victories cost them this is why monsters matter a dragon is not merely a creature it is appetite made flesh a demon is not merely evil it is corrupted reason a wizard is not merely powerful he is accountable for how knowledge reshapes the world fantasy externalizes inner conflict so that it can be confronted honestly enchantment design and worldbuilding as meaning worldbuilding is often mistaken for accumulation more maps more lore more names true worldbuilding is designselective intentional disciplined the world of elsuon was not built to impress it was built to withstand interrogation every culture every blade every order of warriors exists for a reason enchantment is not decoration it is metaphysics made visible magic operates within boundaries because power without structure collapses into tyranny this is as true in fiction as it is in history ai art games gaming communities and visual design now allow fantasy worlds to be explored across mediumsnovels serial releases audio narration and video interpretation these tools are neither saviors nor threats they are instruments what matters is whether the underlying story has integrity noble ends is a serial because transformation does not occur in a single volume redemption unfolds faith matures morality fractures and reforms serial fantasy honors timeallowing readers to witness change rather than merely be told it occurred faith redemption and reason fantasy has always wrestled with faith even when pretending not to whether through angels descending in fire or ancient elves retreating into memory the question remains the same is the world governed by meaning or merely by force noble ends answers without preaching salvation is possible but never cheap redemption is offered but not imposed reason matters justice matters hope matters precisely because it is fragile this is where fantasy outpaces realism realism often mistakes cynicism for wisdom fantasy remembers that despair is not insightit is exhaustion skywens transformation is not merely physical it is moral and spiritual she does not become nobler by acquiring power but by accepting obligation she learns that salvation is not selfexpression but alignmentbetween body will and purpose why this story now the writing community often asks why another fantasy novel is necessary the answer is simple because the questions have not changed who deserves power what must be sacrificed to wield it can beauty survive violence can courage coexist with mercy can identity endure transformation fantasy persists because reality does not answer these questions cleanly epic fantasy gives them room dark fantasy gives them teeth high fantasy gives them scale noble ends exists because stories still matterbecause heroes still teach women still carry worlds on their shoulders swords still symbolize choice and hope remains the most radical act available to us the world of elsuon is not an escape it is a mirrorpolished sharpened and offered without apology and like all true fantasy it asks not what you believebut what you are willing to become

is stranger things an adaptation of the red book by cg jung ive been diving deep into the visual and psychological parallels of season 5 and im convinced the duffer brothers arent just inspired by 80s horrorthey are adapting cg jungs the red book liber novus into the ultimate psychic topography if we look at the show through the lens of jungian individuation and freuds structural model the upside down ceases to be a parallel dimension and becomes a physical map of a broken mind 1 the visual link the sketches the aesthetic jungs red book is famous for its terrifyingly beautiful surreal paintings of dragons tentacles and fiery abysses created during his active imagination sessions the imagery the pulsing red of the abyss the sprawling vines acting like neural synapses and the eyeless monsters the shadow are straight out of jungs visions of the collective unconscious the sketchbook henry creels childhood drawings of the mind flayer are his version of the red book like jung he drew his demons to give them form but where jung sought healing henry sought a dark individuation 2 the 12 archetypes the 12 victims jung identified 12 core archetypes in our theory henry isnt just killing kids he is abducting the archetypes of his own mind to stabilize his wormhole the einsteinrosen bridge the 12 victims on the pain tree these represent the 12 pillars of a healthy psyche the innocent the explorer the caregiver etc by entombing them in the abyss henry freezes his development in 1959 the 12 friends the party they represent the living archetypes eleven is the anima the bridge to the soul dustin is the sage mike is the herobond and will is the wounded child 3 the freudian topography i explained that idea here henry fell into a coma in 1959 his mind is a space between space and time the abyss the id the primal nihilistic source of power mind flayer hawkins russia the superego the social straitjacket and the punishing authority shaped by his 1959 fear of the red menace the upside down the ego a decaying bridge where he tries to force the id into the superego 4 the simultaneity evidence in s4e07 nancy sees henrys past in the abyss 1986 at the exact same time eleven relives it in the lab 1979 this isnt time travel its simultaneity of consciousness every layer of henrys brainmemory camazotz trauma the lab and primal drive the abyssis happening at once conclusion the merge in season 5 isnt just a physical invasion its a total psychotic break like the wedding of the concious and unconcous also in henry wants the id to swallow the superego the battle for hawkins is a battle for the sovereignty of a mind

things mathematicians might call it selfreferencewhen an object refers to itself programmersrecursion cryptographersa checksum that contains its own key but whatever you call itit is strange strange because such numbers are rare the overwhelming majority of dates when converted to base43 do not contain 43 in their notation you can verify this take any random day calculate its mjd convert it to base43 most likely you will not see 43 there strange because this is a specific date not an abstract numberbut victory day russias main holiday a date celebrated with parades on red square remembered by millions that defines national identity strange because fortythree is not a random number in russian history it is the year of the stalingrad victory iv nineteen fortythree on february second of that year field marshal friedrich paulus surrendered to soviet forces in the basement of a stalingrad department store with him capitulated the remnants of the 6th german armyabout ninety thousand men exhausted frostbitten starving a quarter million had perished in the encirclement several hundred thousand moreon the approaches to the city the battle of stalingrad was the largest battle in human history by casualties on both sides by the ferocity of the fighting by the consequences for the course of the war after stalingrad the german army no longer advanced it only retreatedfor two years through ukraine and belarus through poland and hungary all the way to berlin stalingrad is nineteen fortythree a year encoded by two digits four and three v now look at the map find volgogradas stalingrad is now called the coordinates of the city center 4843 north latitude fortyeight degrees fortythree minutes the number fortythree is literally written in the geographic coordinates of the city where the decisive battle of nineteen fortythree occurred coincidence perhaps coordinates are determined by geography not history the city was founded where the volga makes a bend where there was a convenient crossing where trade routes converged no one chose the coordinatesthey simply are what they are and yetthey are what they are 4843 vi let us continue our journey across the map find a paradigm shift by james low once we see that our thoughts are coming and going our feelings are coming and going the sensations in my body are coming and going then once we begin to see that that the world is dynamic then we have a paradigm shift i am moving in a moving world to try and stabilize a moving world doesnt make sense i need to become better at movement i need to move with circumstances i dont know what is going to happen so i give up the fantasy of control that doesnt mean that i go to the other extreme to feeling out of control i am in the middle present with what is occurring and moving with that sometimes coming forward sometimes giving space always being in connection then we start to see that we are not an autonomous individual that we are a participant part of what is already here i can relax and live through my senses through my embodied being with the world as it shows itself i can allow myself to be as i manifest i can feel sad hopeless hopeful whatever arises i can notice what this does to my body and how it positions me closer to other people or further away the more i allow this display of expression the less i identify with a definition of me the more aware i am that this is all just potential manifesting where does this potential come from it is the mind displaying itself what is the mind then we start to explore is the mind a thing is the mind inside my body is it outside my body is it big is it small through relaxing into the meditation and making these explorations again and again we start to get a feel of the unspeakable mystery of existence now there is no point to solving a mystery unless its in a crime book mystery is something to be entered into james low

ultimate review autechre music as cognitive architecture within the landscape of experimental electronic music autechre occupies a singular position a duo that doesnt compose tracks so much as construct systems sonic ecosystems sensitive machines their work is not meant to be listened to in the traditional sense but rather inhabited the way one inhabits an architecture or a mental space far from emotional narration or expressive melody their music offers an experience in which emotion is never given but emerges it doesnt reside in melody or harmony but in the relations between elements tensions collisions resonances microevents autechre doesnt tell stories they set processes in motion an aesthetic of structure form as emotion where popular music seeks identification autechre seeks transformation their abstraction is not a withdrawal but a strategy by removing familiar reference points they compel the listener to reconfigure their listening to invent a new relationship to sound in theoretical terms their music functions like an aesthetic object in serge tisserons sense an object that does not deliver explicit emotional content but instead gives form to tensions affects and shadow zones in a way that is transformed enough to be bearable chaos is never raw it is structured geometrized architected autechre takes the formless and gives it formnot a comforting form but a thinkable one sound as space a phenomenology of listening listening to autechre is less a musical experience than a phenomenological one you dont listen to a track you traverse a space granular textures fractured rhythms and unpredictable pulses create an environment in which the listener must constantly readjust perception there is no center no hierarchy no guiding line it is music that forces you to think with the body to feel with the intellect to navigate a terrain where the usual categoriesmelody rhythm harmonydissolve one could say their work proposes a topological listening sound becomes terrain relief matter to explore a nonhuman emotional grammar one of autechres strengths is their ability to propose emotion without affect no sadness no joy no anger but intensity tension presence it is a nonhuman or rather posthuman emotionality that bypasses the usual codes of expressive music it operates through density speed granularity repetition rupture saturation scarcity autechre invent a new emotional grammar where affect is no longer represented but generated by structure itself a music that transforms the listener what fundamentally distinguishes autechre is not only their radical aesthetic but the way their work acts upon the listener this is not music one consumes it is music that modifies it reconfigures modes of listening perceptual habits and sometimes even emotional structures the experience is not passive it is transformative 1 a reconfiguration of listening autechre dismantles the reflexes of conventional listening searching for melody anticipating progression waiting for a climax recognizing motifs none of these strategies apply the listener must unlearn in order to learn anew listening becomes an active cognitive act requiring one to map shifting structures detect unstable patterns accept unpredictability surrender to the internal logic of the sonic system this reconfiguration is already a transformation 2 a productive destabilization autechre destabilizes but this destabilization is productive not destructive by removing familiar anchors they open a space where the listener can feel differently think differently perceive differently it is an edge experience pushing the listener beyond habitual perceptual frameworks toward a more open attentive and flexible mode of awareness 3 affective transformation through abstraction though autechre avoids explicit emotional cues the listener often emerges deeply affected the reason is simple abstraction acts as a neutral mirror a space where affects can project shift and transform emotion is not delivered it emerges this emergent affect is a form of inner transformation allowing the listener to encounter emotional zones inaccessible through conventional expressive music 4 a process of subjectivation autechre does not offer music about something they offer music that produces a subject the listener becomes the author of the experience by organizing chaos finding coherence in instability constructing meaning in abstraction elaborating internal order in response to external disorder it is music that creates subjectivity not by telling a story but by enabling the listener to become the story 5 cognitive transformation thinking otherwise autechre proposes a form of nonconceptual thinking thinking through sound through structure through sensation their music complexifies attention trains the ear to tolerate ambiguity encourages pattern recognition in the unpredictable opens a mental space where logic becomes topological rather than linear it is music that teaches the mind to operate differently 6 aesthetic transformation learning to love the unknown perhaps the most profound transformation is aesthetic autechre teaches the listener to love what they do not understand in a culture saturated with instantly legible music autechre offers an aesthetics of opacity complexity and unfamiliarity and gradually the listener learns to find pleasure beauty freedom in the unknown this is a rare transformation the reshaping of taste itself conclusion autechre or music as thought autechre is not a band it is a method a way of treating sound as conceptual material a way of making music into a space where one can get lost find oneself and be transformed their work is not emotional yet it enables emotion it is not narrative yet it enables meaning it is not human yet it enables humanity a humanity discovered through abstraction complexity and freedom autechre does not compose tracks they build inner architectures and that may be the most radical form of music today

noori his dorpa band saagama 2022 soundtrack of a revolution the rise of sudans beja music a collaboration with a new york record label is enabling the sounds of the countrys eastern desert to reach a global audience by mee correspondent published date 18 july 2022 1250 bst the outbreak of a revolution is one of the most transformative and socially vibrant processes that can occur in human societies so when the members of ostinato records an independent record label in new york heard that a revolution had broken out in sudan in late 2018 they travelled to the country as soon as they could to capture it we can now not only showcase our music to the world but we can also use it to shed light on our ongoing struggle noureddine jaber musician through friends and colleagues in the country they learned that the revolution which forced the fall of former leader omar hassan albashir after three decades in power within just five months had opened the door to a fascinating musical revitalisation sudans dynamic music scene was a victim of the suffocating and socially conservative bashir era with the norms of the previous decades being challenged ostinato members did not want to miss the opportunity to record it when the revolution started i was told music was playing a very central role vik sohonie founder of ostinato records told middle east eye people were chanting all kinds of new music and music that people were not expressing before the outbreak of the covid19 pandemic however cut short their initial plans to travel to sudan but when they heard the news last october of the military coup that put an end to the fragile transition in the country and the new tension that had opened up between the generals and the prodemocracy opposition they decided to head quickly to khartoum the members of ostinato records knew well where they were going in 2018 the label had released an album called two niles to sing a melody which traced the golden age of sudanese music the work included the likes of legendary late nubian musician mohammed wardi one of the regions most notable influential performers and activists of the 20th century this time the surprise for sohonie came from a very different channel tiktok scrolling through the social video app shortly after landing in sudan he found a clip recorded by a mysterious band from port sudan a city on the red sea coast that left him fascinated the beautiful thing about tiktok is that the algorithm is very localised sohonie said so while we were scrolling we saw a very badly shot video of this band playing and i just thought these guys are incredible he then decided to dive into it by tracking down the band alongside other artists from the region and putting together an album comprised of their work the result has been the production of the first ever known international release of beja music a genre native to sudans eastern desert region which is home to the beja people released in june 2022 the album beja power features the local outfit that sohonie found on tiktok we recorded it during the coup and the protests the producer said the leader of the band that circulated in the sudanese tiktok universe was noureddine jaber also known as noori one day in the late 1990s this sudanese musician ventured near the scrapyards of his hometown of port sudan and by surprise found the wellpreserved neck of a guitar which sohonie noted was a rare instrument in this area soon after his father attalmula jaber shakak a renowned local instrumentalist gave noori a vintage tambour from the 1970s a traditional fourstringed instrument strummed across the region thanks to his manual skills the young man forged the two pieces into a unique electrified tambourguitar probably the only one in existence noori was only 18 at the time but with that unique instrument in hand and driven by a passionate cause he set out on a mission to keep the littleknown beja music scene alive the desire to preserve beja music came even before the instrument noori told mee noori says the need to preserve beja culture motivates his music ostinata records the beja are an ancient multitribal people who trace their origins back to ancient egypt and the nubian kingdom of kush their roots are in a vast semidesert territory that lies between the nile valley and the red sea coast covering eastern sudan one of the main features the beja have in common is the bedawiye language which is classified by most linguists as a cushitic language a branch of the afroasiatic language family however many also speak tigre and arabic depending on the area they live in like the rest of sudans indigenous and peripheral peoples the beja have traditionally been a group persecuted and marginalised by central governments in khartoum resulting in profound political social and economic inequalities compared to the countrys centre bashirs regime in particular motivated by a mixture of arab ethnocentrism islamism and opportunism launched a fierce campaign against the beja people that among other things tried to erase their language and culture off the map bashir wanted to obliterate the beja culture and replace it he said we were lazy backwards people with lice and of no use to the state noori said this then became a policy of neglect he added even after the fall of the former dictator in mid2019 little changed in the area the most obvious evidence of neglect in eastern sudan is that the area remains one of the poorest in the country despite being home to its main port port sudan and having fertile land rich in mineral resources such as gold another more subtle yet catastrophic consequence the members of ostinato records noted is the precarious state of the rich and diverse beja culture and music few old beja recordings were produced in this context and even fewer if any remain to obliterate beja you have to destroy the language the culture and the music or at least ensure it does not reach anywhere noori said and it was precisely with the aim of trying to reverse this delicate trend that noori decided to form noori his dorpa band in 2006 with five other members from different parts of sudan beja music has power because it is made in our mountainous region dorpa means mountain and the echoes of the mountain amplify the music and give it strength noori noted beja people are known for their manufacturing of weapons knives swords many people carry these with them every day it is a symbol of strength he added for me i made the tamboguitar also as a symbol of strength and the ability to preserve our culture he added now the album produced by ostinato records featuring noor his dorpa band is intended to become the latest contribution from the red sea region to the worlds musical corpus for the first beja album to travel not just the world but also sudan is a milestone in beja history noori said we can now not only showcase our music to the world but we can also use it to shed light on our ongoing struggle he added beja power features six tracks that take the listener to another time and space filled with long rarely heard melodies in its own way the album aims to become a living archive of the best and most heartfelt beja songs each having been composed at a different time in their millennial history this music is very deep its the feeling of a traveller omer alghali coproducer of the album and founder of the khartoumbased ogali creative events told mee the music has been perfected over many generations to become a very refined sound noori explained combining styles such as electric soul blues jazz and rock even hints of country the results are styles and chords that could well be tuareg ethiopian peruvian or thai members of ostinato records explained its unique because of the rhythm melody and the composition of the music alghali noted its a fusion of many different parts of the world in one melody he added for sohonie the new album is also a soundtrack to the revolution in sudan firstly because the beja people have actively participated in the countrys protests as they have continued to fight against the discriminatory policies of the central government and secondly without the revolution the space for music from the periphery would unlikely have opened i think that if the events of the last two to three years didnt happen i dont know if this music would have come out sohonie said noori agrees we started the band in 2006 but after 2019 we felt more empowered to present our music he said we began playing a lot more in khartoum and people recorded us playing and put it on social media and opportunities came noori added alghali also believed that the album will also raise awareness about the beja and for people to go beyond music and explore their history and struggle and although he acknowledged there is still little awareness among the public and a lack of government support for this music he considered the opportunity given to noori his dorpa band as something that is unique noori has been trying to promote his music for many years but he didnt have a good opportunity to take it to the world alghali said now he has a good chance he concluded its a golden opportunity middleeasteyenet

embracing the beautiful blank page a deep reflection on the power of being undefined we all hate the feeling of being undefined its that space after a major endinga career pivot the end of a long relationship or simply realizing the goal you were chasing no longer fits your soul society tells us we must always have a fiveyear plan a label and a clear direction when we lose that definition the anxiety hits hard and we desperately try to rush the mapping process but what if being undefined is not a state of failure but the most crucial fertile ground for genuine growth the power of the liminal space when something is defined it is fixed it has limits it is done the undefined is the state of infinite potential it is the blank canvas before the masterpiece the cleared garden bed waiting for the perfect seeds in selfimprovement we often focus so much on the becoming that we forget the necessity of the unbecoming being undefined means you are not bound by old labels old expectations or old versions of self your energy is liberated currently unassigned and ready to be channeled into a more authentic direction practical action navigating the undefined with compassion if you are currently sitting in this uncomfortable undefined space here are three actionable shifts you can make to leverage this powerful phase 1 define the feeling not the title stop pressuring yourself to name the next job the next city or the next identity instead define the qualities and feelings you need next do you need to feel more secure more creative more free use these feelings as your compass the specific map the job title will appear once you know the direction the feeling action step write down three core feelings you need to cultivate in the next 6 months use these to guide small daily choices 2 explore with zero stakes when you are undefined your task is to gather data this isnt the time for massive commitments but for gentle exploration sign up for a class youd never take try a new hobby for 30 minutes read a book in a genre outside your norm you are simply feeding your internal system new information without the pressure of finding the answer action step commit to one lowstakes purely curious activity this week if it feels bad you gained definition you learned what you dont want if it feels good you found a clue 3 practice radical presence the art of the pause the defined self lives in the future the plan or the past the label the undefined self exists purely in the present moment the anxiety comes from trying to project definition onto a moment that is meant to be observed when you feel lost pause breathe deeply and notice three things you can hear see and touch action step dedicate 5 minutes daily to simply being in the ambiguity dont plan dont worry just exist this teaches your nervous system that the undefined state is safe your life is currently drafting a masterpiece dont rush the drafting embrace the quiet creative pause of being undefined you are not lost you are simply becoming ready
